chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Zur'ah ibn Muhammad, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And before that they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieve.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Jews found in their Books that Muhammad's (peace be upon him and his family) emigration would be between Ayr and Uhud, so they went out seeking the place. They passed by a mountain called Hadaad, so they said,

Those who were at Tayma longed for some of their brothers. A Bedouin from Qays passed by them, so they hired him. He said to them, 'I will pass with you between Ayr and Uhud.' They said to him, 'When you pass by these two, let us know.' When he was in the middle of the land of Medina, he said to them, 'That is Ayr and this is Uhud.' So they descended from the backs of his camels and said, 'We have achieved our goal, so we have no need for your camels; go wherever you wish.'

And they wrote to their brothers who were at Fadak and Khaybar, 'We have found the place, so come to us.' They wrote back to them, 'We have settled in the houses and acquired wealth, and we are close to you. So when that happens, we will quickly come to you.'

So they acquired wealth in the land of Medina. When their wealth increased, it reached Tubba', so he attacked them. They fortified themselves against him, so he besieged them. They felt sympathy for the weak ones of Tubba's companions, so they threw dates and barley to them at night. When that reached Tubba', he felt sympathy for them and granted them amnesty, so they came down to him.

He said to them, 'I have grown fond of your land and do not see myself except as remaining in you.' They said to him, 'That is not for you, for it is the emigration of a Prophet, and it is not for anyone until that happens.' He said to them, 'I will leave behind among you members of my family, so when that happens, they will support him and help him.'

So he left behind two tribes, Al-Aws and Al-Khazraj. When they multiplied there, they used to take the wealth of the Jews. The Jews used to say to them, 'But if Muhammad is sent, he will surely drive you out from our houses and our wealth.'

So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), the Helpers believed in him, but the Jews denied him. And this is the Statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And before that they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieve.'
When there came to them that which they did not recognize, they disbelieved in him. So the curse of Allah is on the disbelievers.

key_terms.يَسْتَفْتِحُونَ: They used to pray for victory

ai.seo_question: How did the Jews' knowledge of the Prophet's emigration location lead to their denial of him?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the historical context of the Quranic verse 'And before that, they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved' (2:89), detailing how Jewish tribes identified the specific location of the Prophet's Hijra between Ayr and Uhud. It narrates the subsequent arrival of Tubba' and the establishment of the Aws and Khazraj tribes, who later became the Ansar, contrasting their acceptance of the Prophet with the Jews' denial upon his arrival. This narrative underscores the Shia scholarly view of 'Tahqiq al-Ma'rifah' (knowing the truth upon recognition) and the subsequent 'Kufr' (disbelief) of those who knew but rejected.

en.hubeali: H 14929 – Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al-Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al-Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Zur’at Bin Muhammad, from Abu Baseer, who has said:
Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Statement of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic: “[2:89] and before that they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieve”.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Jews had found in their Book that Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> would emigrate between Ayr and Ohad, so they went out look for these places. They passed by a mountain called Hadaad, so they said, ‘Hadaad and Ohad are one and the same’. So they dispersed upon that. Some of them encamped at Tayma and some of them at Fadak, and some of them at Khyber’.

The ones who were at Tayma longed to be with some of their brothers. A Bedouin from Qays, passed by them so they hired (a camel) from him and he said to them, ‘I shall pass with you in between Ayr and Ohad’. They said to him, ‘When you pass by these two, point these two places out to us. So when he was in the middle of the land of Al-Medina, he said to them, ‘That is Ayr and this is Ohad’. So they descended from the backs of his camels and said, ‘We have reached where we wanted to be, therefore we do not have any need for your camels, and so you can go to wherever you like’.

And they wrote to their brothers who were at Fadak and Khyber, ‘We have got to the place so come to us’. They wrote back to them, ‘We have settled in the houses and acquired assets, and there is no one closer to us than you are. So when that event transpires, we would quickly come to you’.

They acquired assets in the land of Al-Medina. When their wealth increased, it (news) reached Tubba and he attacked them. They fortified themselves from him, so he surrounded them. They felt sympathetic towards the weak ones of Tubba and they would throw the dates and the barley towards them at night. So (the news of) that reached Tubba, and he sympathised with them and granted them amnesty. They came down to him.

He said to them, ‘I have come to like your city and would like to reside among you’. So they said to him, ‘It is not for you to dwell in that place, for a Prophet<sup>saww</sup> would be emigrating and that is not for anyone until that happens’.

He said to them, ‘I will leave behind among you members of my family, so when that happens, they would support him<sup>saww</sup> and help him<sup>saww</sup>’.
So he left behind two tribes, Al-Aws and Al-Khazraj. So when they multiplied, they used to take the wealth of the Jews and the Jews used to say to them, ‘But, when Muhammad<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> is Sent, he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> would take you all out from our houses and our wealth’.

So when Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Sent Muhammadsaww, the Helpers believed in himsaww, but the Jews denied himsaww, and it is the Statement of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic: “[2:89] and before that they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieve
, but when there came to them (Prophet) that which they did not recognize, they disbelieved in him; so Allah's curse is on the unbelievers.”
en.sarwar: 482. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said:
‘I asked Abu Abdullah (a.s.) about the Statement of Allah (azwj) Blessed and High: “[2:89] and before that they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieve,

but when there came to them (Prophet) that which they did not recognize, they disbelieved in him”. He (a.s.) said: ‘A people who were in between (the era of) Muhammad (saww) and Isa (as), and they would inform the idol worshippers about the promised Prophet (saww), and they were saying, ‘When the Prophet (saww) comes out, he (saww) would break your idols, and will do this with you, and that with you’. However, when the Rasool Allah (saww) came out, they denied him (saww)’.
